The assumptions behind the numbers.

These are planning examples using published university rates, a transfer scenario and an editable outside-course budget. They are not complete degree quotes or approved course plans. They exclude financial aid, most fees, books and living costs; WGU’s term price includes its required resource charge.

For per-credit and semester-band schools, the same study load is used before and after transfer. Short final terms use the relevant part-time price. For UMPI and WGU, paid terms are separate assumptions you can edit: fewer transfer requirements only reduce cost if they let you avoid paid terms. Outside study time and school processing are additional.

Some schools allow more institutional transfer than low-cost course-provider credit. TESU and Charter Oak’s 114-credit possibilities cannot be priced as 114 cheap ACE/NCCRS credits. WGU’s Project Management example retains 32 nontransferable CUs, so its example is capped at 88 transferred CUs. UMPI’s 90-credit possibility follows from a 120-credit degree with at least 30 UMPI credits, rather than a universal fixed transfer cap.

What does the outside-course budget cover?

The default $2,000 is an editable planning allowance for course memberships, course/exam charges and related outside-credit costs. It does not mean that $2,000 buys an approved 90-credit basket at every college. Required major courses, higher-level work, labs, taxes or additional paid months can change it. Consult each provider’s current prices and obtain course approvals before purchasing.

Liberty University · Online

Up to 90 of 120 credits. At least 25% of the degree and major/minor remains with Liberty. Actual outside-credit placement depends on the exact online program.

The $410 rate requires at least 12 credits in each billed semester; semesters of 11 or fewer credits use $475 per credit. The example excludes the $349 technology fee per semester, the $100 degree-completion fee, and other applicable charges. The catalog’s $38/credit Inclusive Access charge is waived for online undergraduates and is not added here.

The calculation uses 15 credits per billed semester. Many online courses use eight-week subterms, but full-time pricing is determined by the total semester load, not by treating every subterm as a separate semester.

A pricing and transfer-policy illustration, not a complete online course-by-course degree audit. The existing residential Liberty draft does not automatically map to an online program.

Southern New Hampshire University · Online

Up to 90 of 120 credits. Eligible college credit and approved prior learning can combine toward the transfer limit. The university decides which requirements they meet.

The example excludes the $100 conferral fee, books/materials, and other applicable costs. No application fee is added. Aid, employer support, and discounts are not modeled.

At two three-credit courses per eight-week term, 120 credits model 20 terms and 30 credits model five terms. SNHU offers six eight-week terms per year; the modeled teaching weeks are not a promised graduation date.

A tuition and transfer-policy example. DegreeSteps has not supplied a complete approved course map for this SNHU degree.

Thomas Edison State University · Online

Up to 114 with eligible mixed credit. The 114-credit possibility requires the conditional six-credit Edison Accelerate route and eligible source types. ACE/NCCRS credit is limited to 90 combined. This cost example uses 90 outside credits and 30 TESU credits on the standard route.

Nonresident pricing is used. Registration for 9–18 credits receives the $4,652 flat term rate; smaller term loads use $584 per credit. The example excludes the $50 application fee, $98 graduation audit, books, and other charges. It does not include an Edison Accelerate fee because this is the standard tuition scenario. NJ/PA resident prices differ.

At 15 credits per billed 12-week term, 120 credits model eight terms and 30 credits model two terms. Monthly starts and selected accelerated courses can offer flexibility; actual sequencing, assessments, approval, and availability determine the calendar.

A standard-route tuition illustration. The current TESU degree draft is a partial course map; the comparison does not convert its conditional course choices into school-approved awards or implement the reduced-course Accelerate alternative.

Charter Oak State College · Online

Up to 114 from four-year colleges. The 114-credit four-year-institution ceiling differs from the 87-credit two-year-institution limit and the 90-credit non-collegiate course-provider limit. This example uses 90 approved outside credits.

The example includes tuition at $329 per credit but excludes $18.75 materials per credit, $230 student services and $75 technology per semester, the $50 application fee, and other charges. A $150 enrollment deposit is credited toward tuition and must not be counted a second time.

The illustration assumes 15 credits per semester. Charter Oak offers multiple course lengths, including eight-, five-, and fifteen-week formats. Cornerstone is normally first term and Capstone is taken in the final semester with advisor approval, so scheduling remains a separate check.

A tuition and transfer-policy example with 30 Charter Oak credits remaining. DegreeSteps does not yet supply a complete approved course-by-course Charter Oak map.

University of Maine at Presque Isle · Online

30 credits minimum at UMPI. UMPI states no fixed incoming-credit limit. Ninety possible outside credits is arithmetic for a 120-credit degree with 30 required UMPI credits, not a published universal transfer cap. Major and upper-level requirements still apply.

The $1,800 rate buys an eight-week undergraduate YourPace session; it is not a per-credit price. Basic materials are generally included, but the comparison excludes any applicable extra supplies, personal costs, and other fees. Campus YourPace options can have additional charges and are not modeled.

The default paid-session scenario is eight sessions without transfer versus two after approved transfer, corresponding illustratively to 15 credits per session. Paid-session counts are editable assumptions; transfer credit does not automatically remove sessions, and outside learning/approval time is additional.

A paid-session cost scenario, not a completion prediction or approved 90-credit degree map. The dated $1,800 session rate is used instead of older total-degree marketing examples.

Western Governors University · Online

32 CUs stay with this WGU program. WGU’s institutional ceiling is 75%, but the current Project Management pathway lists 32 nontransferable CUs. Eighty-eight is therefore a theoretical program upper bound, not an established 88-CU ACE basket. This degree’s actual evaluated transfer amount can be lower.

Each modeled six-month term includes $3,830 tuition plus the required $200 e-books/resource fee, totaling $4,030. Unlike the other tuition-only rows, this known resource fee is included in the term price. The $65 application fee and any other applicable costs are excluded; possible waivers are not assumed.

The default explicit scenario uses eight paid six-month terms before transfer and three after it, consistent with roughly 15 CUs per paid term and 32 CUs remaining. These counts are editable assumptions, not WGU’s program outline or a prediction; transfer helps tuition only if it reduces the paid terms actually needed.

A program-specific paid-term illustration, not a complete WGU degree audit. The 110-CU B.S. Business Management degree has different requirements and pricing and must not be substituted into this 120-CU Project Management example.
